about:
SlackHacks -- Essential Quality of Life Tweaks to Native Blizzard UIs
=====================================================================

This is *yet another* "Quality of Life" WoW addon with various small features and tweaks, but my focus is on making my changes look like they're part of the native Blizzard UI.

Everything is a module.

Everything is optional.

Everything is off by default. (Please read all the options!)

If you've used Plumber or Leatrix, this is similar, but I'm trying *very* hard to make it look like Blizzard wrote all the features I'm providing. (Because of this, it is probably incompatible with full UI redesigns like Ellesmere UI.) 

## Why make this? Why make another QoL addon...?

I've been programming in general since 1998, and *professionally* for almost 20 years, and right now, I'm sorely depressed at seeing how all the "new" addons are slopified junk generated by Claude, or how many existing addons have turned buggy and are now eating CPU because developers have given up on quality.

Am I using Copilot for some of it? *Yes.* But I'm using my years of experience to make sure it's good output, and once I finish any given module, I spend time *manually* reviewing and polishing it. As soon as I'm done with all the features, and before I release this into the public CurseForge page, I will review ***all*** the code and make sure all of it is to the quality I would *professionally* feel confident and proud of releasing.

I get *why* we're all using Copilot today: Blizzard has documented nothing and it's a struggle to make even the most "simple" sounding things. But if you're using Claude and "vibing" your addons 100%, you should be embarrassed.

## Contributions

Anything that isn't slop generated that fits with the philosophy of the addon.

## Build and release configuration

Shared, non-secret build and release defaults live in
[`scripts/defaults.env`](https://github.com/Slackwise/SlackHacks/blob/dev/scripts/defaults.env), so a fresh clone can build
without any local configuration. For local overrides and credentials, create an
ignored `.env` in the repository root by copying
[`.env.example`](https://github.com/Slackwise/SlackHacks/blob/dev/.env.example) and replacing the placeholder values with each
developer's own deployment tokens. For example, run `cp .env.example .env` from
the repository root in Bash.

Do not commit `.env` or put API tokens in `scripts/defaults.env`. The deployment
scripts also support Proton Pass; set the appropriate `PROTON_PASS_ITEM_*`
values in `.env` if your item names differ from the defaults. Environment
variables already set by the shell or CI/CD environment take precedence over
both files, so CI can inject its own configuration and secrets.

### Updating icon names

Icon search uses only file IDs and names extracted from the public-domain
LibRPMedia submodule in `dist/LibRPMedia`; the library is not shipped or loaded.
Run `perl scripts/update-icon-names.pl` to fetch its latest commit and regenerate
`IconNames.lua`. Use `--no-update` to regenerate from the checked-out revision
without fetching. Commit both the generated file and the updated submodule
revision. The build refuses to reset an unstaged submodule revision.

### Publishing and retrying releases

Run `perl scripts/release.pl` from a clean development branch after committing
the version bump and a non-empty `## v<VERSION>` section in `CHANGELOG.md`.
The script merges into `prod`, preferring the source branch on conflicts while
retaining non-conflicting `prod` changes. It creates an immutable version tag, atomically
pushes `prod` and the tag, and deploys that production checkout before restoring
your original branch (also on deployment failure). `--no-push` prepares only
the local release and never deploys. `--force` no longer bypasses dirty-worktree
checks or overwrites tags.

Rerun the same release command after a partial failure: an existing tag is
resumed, not recreated, provided the source has no commits outside that release
and production has not advanced or diverged. New development needs a version
bump rather than retagging a published release.

To intentionally include new commits in the same version, commit the changes
and changelog on `dev`, then run `perl scripts/release.pl --rerelease`.
This is an explicit exception to immutable releases: it merges into `prod`,
moves the version tag only when the release commit changes, and atomically
pushes the branch and tag using a tag-specific force-with-lease. Concurrent
remote tag changes reject the push rather than being overwritten. It does not
force-push `prod`, permit dirty worktrees, or allow releasing an older version
when a newer tag exists. `--dry-run` previews and `--no-push` prepares locally;
retry either with `--rerelease` to finish publishing the revised release.

The flag is forwarded to both deployers. GitHub's existing release notes are
updated and a mismatched ZIP is deleted and uploaded again (there is a window
without the ZIP if upload fails; rerun the same command to finish).
CurseForge receives a **new file** for the revised commit; the API cannot replace
the old file in place. Archive/delete the old file manually on CurseForge.
Confirmed uploads of the same commit are still skipped, and uncertain attempts
remain blocked, even with `--rerelease`. Receipts for each revision are retained.
For standalone deployment of the already-pushed revision, use
`bash scripts/deploy.sh --rerelease`.

For standalone deployment, check out the release tag or matching `prod` commit
and run `bash scripts/deploy.sh` (or either individual deployment script).
Both deployers verify a clean checkout, the exact pushed `origin/prod` tip, and
the pushed version tag **before building or uploading**. Dry runs perform these
read-only remote checks too, but do not build, retrieve secrets, or upload.
The CurseForge `--list-versions` command remains available without a release.

Release notes are read from the `## v<VERSION>` section of `CHANGELOG.md` (or
of the file named by `CHANGELOG_FILE`), without the heading. A missing file,
missing section, or empty section is an error.
GitHub's separate `generate_release_notes` feature is disabled so commit-derived
notes are not appended; `GENERATE_RELEASE_NOTES` is no longer used.
JSON request bodies and CurseForge metadata are sent from UTF-8 files to avoid
Windows command-line quoting and length problems.

Retries reuse a checksum-verified build for the same commit and packaging
configuration. GitHub looks up the existing release, synchronizes its changelog
notes, and skips an already-uploaded archive with a matching SHA-256 digest.
Without `--rerelease`, an asset with a different or unavailable digest is never
deleted and requires manual inspection.

CurseForge upload receipts live in Git's common directory under
`slackhacks-deploy`, outside the worktree. Confirmed uploads are skipped on retry.
Because the legacy upload API has no idempotency key, pending/ambiguous uploads
block retries: inspect the project's files on CurseForge before removing the
specific pending receipt named in the error. Do not remove a receipt for an
upload that succeeded. These receipts are local to the clone; use the same clone
for retries and check CurseForge before publishing from another machine.

Run the release regression tests with `perl scripts/release.t` (or `prove
scripts/release.t`, or the VS Code **Test release scripts** task). They require
Perl, Git, Bash, and curl, and use temporary local repositories and a local
HTTP server, not publishing credentials or live release APIs.

### Version bumps and changelogs

All release notes live in the root `CHANGELOG.md`, newest release first, with
one `## v<VERSION>` section per release and `### Area` subsections. It is kept
in the repository only and is not packaged into the release ZIP.

`perl scripts/bump.pl` increments the TOC version. If `CHANGELOG.md` has no
section for the new version yet, it asks whether to generate one (default yes)
and then whether to use the GitHub Copilot CLI (yes/no; otherwise entries are
built from `Area: description` commit subjects). Pass `--[no-]changelog` /
`--[no-]copilot` to skip the questions, or `--blank` for an empty section to
fill in by hand (it must be filled in before releasing).

`perl scripts/changelog.pl` creates or extends the section for the current TOC
version without bumping. An existing section is appended to: commits made since
that section was last committed (and not already mentioned) are merged into the
matching `### ` areas; other releases' sections are left untouched. If the TOC
version is already tagged, it offers to bump the version first (default yes).
Use `--[no-]bump` and `--[no-]copilot` to skip the questions, and `--dry-run`
to preview.

## Lua development tools

On Windows x64, run `perl scripts/bootstrap.pl` or the VS Code **Bootstrap**
task (requires Perl, `tar`, and internet access) to install the Lua 5.1 bytecode
compiler, StyLua, and Lua Language Server into the repository-local `.bin`
directory. The bootstrap is safe to rerun; installed tools are left in place.
`.bin` is ignored by Git.

The recommended VS Code extensions are listed in `.vscode/extensions.json`.
Lua Language Server uses `.luarc.json`, and StyLua reads `.stylua.toml`.

## Contact

Here, on GitHub. Post an issue.

Otherwise reach me as `@Slackwise` on Discord.

releases.name: SlackHacks v37
releases.notes:
### ListviewBag
- Refactored the Mail flag workflow to match the other flags.
- Redesigned the Mail Queue Quantity window.

releases.name: SlackHacks v36
releases.notes:
### ListviewBag
- Removed needless "One-Time Junk Items" Options list.

releases.name: SlackHacks v35
releases.notes:
### Inventory
- Junk, Auction, and Bank flags can be set Once or Always; one-time flags clear when the item leaves your bags, and remembered Auction and Bank items get their own Options lists.
- Junk flags now distinguish item variants such as item level, quality, upgrade track, and enchants.
- Added a Deposit Bank Flagged Items button to the bank and an optional Auto-Deposit Bank Flagged Items setting.
- Opening the Auction House now locks the Selling View and hides items that can't be auctioned, replacing AH Mode.
- Added Quick Sell to post Auction-flagged items at the Auction House's default price, one click per item.

### Minimap
- Avoid duplicate Addon Compartment entries and restore minimap icons when the option is disabled.
- Fixed SlackHacks' native Addon Compartment entry not responding to clicks and throwing errors on hover.
- Keep addon icons on the square border through redraws and dragging, without losing legacy icons or their native drag behavior.

### Mouse Ring
- Added a Reset Appearance button for the scale, opacity, and color controls.

releases.name: SlackHacks v34
releases.notes:
### Utilities
- Optionally add icon-name search to the Macro and Equipment Set icon pickers.

### Mimimap
- Fixed bug when switching off square mode.

### Inventory
- Added Selling and Gear views with auction prices, equipment comparisons, and client-specific filters.
- Expanded item flags to include Auction, Bank, and Mail, with safeguards against conflicting actions.
- Added saved mail recipients and queued quantities, with automatic preparation of mail batches.
- Added item, binding, and category filters, including configurable Essentials.
- Improved junk-selling controls and the marked-item list.
- Redesigned the bag footer and inventory summary with capacity, currencies, and client-specific supplies.

releases.name: SlackHacks v33
releases.notes:
### Utilities
- Auto-Open Loot Containers: Removed profession knowledge as it cannot be auto-opened without creating a manual button which isn't much better than just clicking it yourself.
